newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain authorises issues of strippable debt.
newsitem.headline: Spain authorises issues of strippable debt.

text.p: The Spanish Economy Ministry said on Friday that the issuance of strippable debt had appeared in the Official Bulletin and had thus been legalised.
The legalisation will help launch the Spanish market for strippable bonds, the Economy minister said.
Later, the Treasury said the first auction of this strippable debt will be launched in July.
In the Bulletin, the Treasury is authorised to obtain medium- and long-term loans from financial institutions in order to give it more freedom to manoeuvre.
Strips and destrips, or recompositions, must be done through the Central Registry with a minimum amount of 50 million pesetas, with an additional amount of 10 million pesetas.

In a separate statement, the Treasury said KSPY that strips and destrips are only possible when the outstanding volume of an issue is at least one trillion pesetas and when the Treasury has authorised an issue as strippable.
